jobs.occupation: DIAS Fellow in Industrial Ecology and Data-Driven Sustainability Assessment
jobs.description:
The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) and the Department of Green Technology at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invite applications for a tenure-track DIAS Fellow position at Assistant Professor level in Industrial Ecology and Data-Driven Sustainability Assessment, with a focus on input-output life cycle assessment methods and big data. The candidate is expected to start during the summer/early fall in 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter, in agreement with the successful candidate. 

We are looking for a researcher with clear potential for research excellence who thrives in and is inspired by interdisciplinary collaboration. The ideal candidate will be expected to contribute to high-quality research in their field while embracing DIAS’s mission of curiosity-driven inquiry and interdisciplinary dialogue. The successful candidate should have a strong and promising research profile, with potential for attracting external research funding, and a demonstrated ability to work across disciplines. The candidate will be attached to both the Department and DIAS and should be prepared to engage in multiple and diverse research environments at SDU. Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard assistant professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research and leadership activities.

Who are we looking for?

The position translates this ambition into a concrete research agenda, because many of the most pressing sustainability questions, such as how consumption in one country drives resource use, emissions and social conditions in another, or how a new technology changes environmental impacts across whole economies, cannot be answered within a single discipline. Industrial ecology addresses these questions by tracing material, energy and monetary flows through global supply chains, drawing on methods and data from engineering, economics and the natural and social sciences. Input-output analysis, built on big data covering production, trade, emissions and resource use and combined with life cycle assessment and material flow analysis, provides the quantitative framework for linking decisions about individual products, technologies and policies to their economy-wide consequences. The Fellow will build this capacity at SDU and use DIAS as a platform to work with researchers in fields such as health, food, energy, economics and political science on questions that cross disciplinary boundaries. Within this ambition, the specific profile is as follows.

We seek an early-career researcher who will advance quantitative sustainability assessment within industrial ecology by developing data-driven environmental-economic and systems models that link global production and consumption to environmental and socioeconomic outcomes. The role includes independent research, research-based teaching and supervision, interdisciplinary collaboration across DIAS and the Department, and development of competitive external funding proposals. Relevant research themes include:

·         environmental and material footprinting of global production and consumption systems;

·         development and application of environmentally extended input–output (EEIO) and multi-regional input–output (MRIO) models and databases, including hybrid physical–monetary systems and transparent, reproducible data workflows;

·         hybrid modelling that combines EEIO analysis with life cycle assessment (LCA), material flow analysis (MFA), econometrics or other quantitative methods;

·         applications to food and resource systems, healthcare systems and medical technologies, the circular economy, energy, infrastructure and other societal systems; and

·         scenario, structural decomposition, uncertainty and econometric analysis for sustainability transitions, policy and decision support.

The ideal candidate should demonstrate:

·         A commitment to engaging in boundary-crossing interdisciplinary research and dialogue.

·         A strong commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration, contributing to research that bridges multiple fields.

·         Strong interest in driving internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition. 

·         Engagement in various forms of research dissemination, including interdisciplinary research and dialogue. 

 

Qualifications

Successful applicants must:

·         Hold a PhD or similar qualifications within relevant fields of industrial ecology, environmental or ecological economics, environmental science or engineering, sustainability science or a closely related field. To qualify for the position as Assistant Professor you must have obtained a PhD or similar degree by the application deadline. 

·         The successful candidate should demonstrate strong competence in EEIO or MRIO analysis, and at least one of the following areas: LCA, MFA, or hybrid modelling; econometric, statistical, or other quantitative methods; and programming, data science, or management of large, heterogeneous datasets.

·         Exhibit curiosity-driven research excellence, thinking beyond traditional boundaries.

·         Be fluent in English.

·         Show potential for attracting external research funding. Experience in applying for external funding and a strong international network are considered comparative advantages.

·         Have research publications that demonstrate their excellence and broad thinking. 

 

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally.   

The Department of Green Technology

The Department of Green Technology at SDU is a dynamic and interdisciplinary research environment focused on developing technologies and strategies for a sustainable future. Our research spans environmental chemistry, process engineering, life cycle thinking, and circular systems. We collaborate closely with industry and public stakeholders to ensure real-world impact and relevance.

This position will be affiliated with SDU Life Cycle Engineering (SDU LCE).

SDU Life Cycle Engineering

SDU LCE uses industrial ecology approaches to reduce environmental impacts and reconcile human development with environmental stewardship. We conduct holistic systems analyses and design studies to characterise and optimise engineering solutions over the long term, considering resource use, energy efficiency, climate and environmental impacts, and economic and socioeconomic performance. At SDU LCE, we develop and apply theory, methods and tools for material flow analysis (MFA), life cycle assessment (LCA), life cycle engineering, energy-system analysis and design, resource-criticality assessment, process integration and techno-economic assessment.

 

Additional information

For further information about being a fellow at DIAS, please contact DIAS director Sten Rynning at +45 6550 2193 or via email at director-dias@sdu.dk.

For further information about SDU Life Cycle Engineering and this position, please contact Head of Centre, Professor Morten Birkved, at morb@igt.sdu.dk.

 

Application, salary, and employment terms

The position is based at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, Department of Green Technology, in Odense and includes regular participation in DIAS and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Employment is governed by the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and the provisions for tenure track assistant professor as described herein. Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

The salary comprises a seniority-based base salary and a centrally agreed supplement.

Additional supplements may be negotiated locally.

As of 1 August 2026, the annual salary for an Assistant Professor is DKK 480,224.96 (salary level 6), consisting of a base salary of DKK 417,456 and a supplement of DKK 62,768.96.

All amounts are stated before tax, before added pension (18.07%), and any additional supplements. Pension contributions are paid by SDU, and both salary components (the annual salary and the supplement) are pensionable. For more details on salary and taxation, please see Further information on salary and taxation.

 

The tenure track programme is aimed at the most talented scholars who have established a high level in their current research and other professional work, and those who possess exceptional potential to achieve the highest international level within their research area.

Candidates enter at the assistant professor level (up to six years) and, upon successful completion, will be promoted to a permanent position as associate professor, subject to a positive assessment by an expert committee.  This evaluation is based on an overall assessment of the candidate's academic achievements and potential.

Indicators of relevant scholarly merits include documented ability to develop an independent and internationally recognized research profile, deliver high-quality teaching and supervision, contribute actively to the academic community, and demonstrate the potential to secure competitive external research funding and build an ambitious research programme. The evaluation may also consider the candidate's contributions to the strategic and organizational development of the department, including a willingness to engage in academic leadership and administrative responsibilities. 

As part of the tenure-track programme, the Assistant Professor is expected to complete SDU's Lecturer Training Programme before the evaluation, unless an equivalent university-level programme has already been completed at another institution.

The programme includes annual performance reviews, a midterm evaluation by an expert panel, and a final academic assessment. If the final assessment is positive, the candidate will progress to a permanent position as associate professor. If the final evaluation is negative, the assistant professor may request one additional assessment within the last six months of employment. The tenure track period may be extended in connection with maternity, paternity, or adoption leave.

Equal opportunity employment
The University of Southern Denmark is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, or any other protected status.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes our staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, are subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position.

Please go to our website for full information on how to apply.

The application deadline is February 28, 2027, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST)

Turn AI ideas into real business value.

At Foxway, we're transforming the way organizations buy, use and reuse technology. As a leading provider of Circular IT solutions, we help businesses extend the lifecycle of technology while reducing both cost and environmental impact.

Now we're taking the next step in how we use AI across our business.

We're looking for an AI Business Partner for one of our business areas Computers & Enterprise (C&E) — a new role dedicated to finding, building and driving AI use cases from idea into daily business use.

This isn't a role for someone who simply advises the business on AI. You'll work hands-on with our teams, turn opportunities into working solutions and help us make sure AI creates **measurable value whether through productivity, cost, margin or new ways of working.

**You'll report to the Business Area President and work closely with our Group-wide AI organization and central AI Engineers.

**Location

**This role can be based in one of our Business Area locations: Braintree, Essex (UK); Bucharest (Romania); or Aarhus (Denmark). Candidates must be located in, and able to work from, one of these locations.

****Where AI meets the business

****Across C&E, we already have ideas for where AI could make a difference, and many more are still waiting to be discovered.

**Your job is to connect the dots.

**You'll work across the business to identify and evaluate opportunities, understand the processes and data behind them, build and test solutions, and help teams put them into everyday use.

Just as importantly, you'll help us understand the business case behind AI: what value should this create, how do we measure it, and how do we make that improvement stick?

****Turn ideas into impact

• Find and frame AI use cases together with teams across C&E, assessing value, feasibility and risk.

• Build and ship working AI solutions using the tools that best fit the problem.

• Take use cases from idea and prototype into daily business use and measurable value.

• Build clear value cases, connecting AI initiatives to productivity, cost, margin or other business outcomes.

• Drive adoption and process change, not just implementation of the technology.

• Maintain an overview of AI ideas and active use cases and help keep delivery moving.

• Work closely with our central AI Engineers when deeper data, integrations, or production engineering are required.

• Share successful approaches across Foxway and help identify opportunities where AI could fundamentally reshape how we work.

• Work within Foxway's AI governance, privacy and security framework and coordinate with C&E IT and Product & Service Management.

****What you bring to the build

****This is an experienced-level role. We’re looking for someone who has already delivered AI solutions in a business environment and can bring that experience into C&E from day one.

You might come from AI or technology consulting, AI transformation, technical project/product management, automation, or a similar hands-on role. More important than your current title is what you've actually done.

You don't need to be an AI Engineer as we have dedicated Engineers for the deep build and technical plumbing. But you should be technical enough to turn an opportunity into something real, rather than stopping at the recommendation.

• Substantial hands-on experience delivering AI solutions in a professional environment, with the technical confidence to build and configure solutions yourself, not only advise on or use AI tools.

• A strong track record of taking AI or automation use cases from idea through build, implementation and adoption, with clear evidence of business value or measurable improvement.

• The ability to understand a business process, identify where AI can genuinely add value and translate that into something practical.

• Enough technical depth to build and configure solutions yourself, while knowing when deeper engineering is needed.

• A working understanding of data, APIs and integrations.

• Strong business judgement and the ability to connect solutions to measurable business outcomes.

• Confidence working with both operational teams and senior stakeholders and driving change across an organization.

• Strong written and spoken English skills, as English is the main working language

****Ready to build what AI can become at C&E?

****This is a new role with the opportunity to help shape how AI is applied across an entire Business Area from the first use cases we deliver today to larger transformations in how we operate tomorrow.

If you like being close to the business, building things, and seeing them actually get used, we'd love to hear from you. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so apply as soon as possible.

To protect candidate data and ensure a fair recruitment process, we do not accept applications via email. Please apply through our official career site.

**For the selected final candidate

**Foxway will conduct a background check as part of our recruitment process, in accordance with applicable local legislation and our internal screening policy. The scope of the check depends on the position and the country in which it is based. You will be informed of the details, and your approval will be requested before any check is initiated.

****How does Foxway operate?

****Foxway is a fast-growing and dynamic organization with an international team of nearly 1,300 people. We operate across multiple countries, with key hubs across Europe.

Foxway’s Recommerce Computers & Enterprise (C&E) focuses on sustainable tech management by the refurbishment and resale of used computer equipment, addressing both environmental and market demand.

Our mission is to make sustainable technology accessible to everyone by extending the life of IT equipment and enabling circular business models.

By joining us, you become part of a purpose-driven, international team that is shaping the future of sustainable workplaces and circular technology.

**Job Description

Your work will shape the reliability and scalability of a platform used by engineers, architects, and data practitioners every day. In return, you will grow your skills in a collaborative environment with real technical depth.

**What You Will Be Doing

The Data Platform IT squad operates with a high degree of technical ownership, and you will work closely with platform users, architects, and fellow engineers to translate real needs into self-service capabilities. The team values pragmatic thinking, open collaboration, and continuous improvement, and you will contribute to shaping how the platform evolves across environments.

**In your day-to-day work, you will:

**

• Design and build scalable capabilities on the Databricks platform across environments

• Develop automation using Infrastructure as Code, primarily Terraform

• Improve CI/CD and release automation using GitHub Enterprise Cloud and related tooling

We look forward to hearing from you!

Build software that supports critical construction decisions. Modernize complex systems. Help shape the future of development at Dalux.

**At Dalux, we develop software used by construction professionals in more than 140 countries. Our Tender product supports the bidding process for construction projects and is closely integrated with the wider Dalux platform.

We are looking for an experienced software developer to join our Tender team, where you will help evolve both the product and its technical foundation.

This is a role for an engineer who enjoys understanding complex systems, improving architecture, and building maintainable software while exploring how AI can change the way we develop it.

**Your role

**As an Experienced Software Developer in Tender, you will take responsibility for complex technical and product problems, from understanding the requirements and designing solutions to implementation and delivery.

You will join a full-stack development team working closely with a Product Manager and Product Designer.

The Tender product combines established functionality with ongoing product development. We are particularly interested in strengthening its architecture, improving modularity, and creating a technical foundation that supports continued evolution.

We expect experienced developers to contribute beyond their individual tasks. You should be comfortable questioning existing approaches, discussing architectural trade-offs, and helping the team make good technical decisions.

Your work will include:

• Designing and implementing complex, maintainable full-stack functionality.

• Contributing to architectural decisions and the technical direction of the Tender product.

• Improving existing code and identifying technical debt that limits maintainability or future development.

• Helping evolve application boundaries, modularity, and the structure of the codebase.

• Balancing technical improvements with ongoing product development and delivery.

• Ensuring that reliability, data security, and software quality remain central to engineering decisions.

• Mentoring and sparring with other developers through technical discussions and code reviews.

• Collaborating with Product Management and Design to understand the problems we are solving and identify effective solutions.

You will have opportunities to influence not only individual features but also how the product and its architecture evolve over time.

**Developing software with AI

**AI-assisted software development is becoming an increasingly important part of how we work at Dalux.

We are actively exploring how AI can improve the development lifecycle, including understanding complex codebases, exploring technical approaches, implementing functionality, generating tests, reviewing code, debugging, and refactoring.

The Tender team is already experimenting with AI-assisted development, and we want experienced developers who can contribute to making these workflows more effective.

Working with an established software system makes engineering judgment particularly important. AI can help developers understand unfamiliar code, investigate dependencies, explore refactoring approaches, and accelerate implementation. But understanding the consequences of changes and maintaining a coherent architecture remain essential responsibilities.

As an experienced developer, we expect you to:

• Actively explore and use AI-assisted development workflows where they improve engineering effectiveness.

• Apply strong technical judgment when reviewing and validating AI-generated solutions.

• Investigate how AI can help with codebase understanding, modernization, testing, and refactoring.

• Share useful approaches with colleagues and help establish sound engineering practices around AI-assisted development.

• Challenge existing development workflows when new approaches offer meaningful improvements.

We see AI as a way to increase the effectiveness of capable engineers, not as a substitute for software engineering fundamentals.

Practical experience with AI-assisted or agentic development is a strong advantage. We particularly value developers who can combine new tools with architectural reasoning, systems thinking, and a clear understanding of the problems they are solving.

**Technologies we work with

**Tender is a full-stack product area primarily built using:

• C# / .NET

• Angular / TypeScript

• Microsoft SQL Server

• Elasticsearch

Our wider platform runs on a distributed cloud architecture using AWS.

Experience with our technologies is useful, but the ability to understand, design, and improve complex software systems matters more than an exact technology match.

**Your background

**We are looking for an experienced software developer who enjoys technical responsibility and is motivated by improving both existing systems and the way software is developed.

We expect that you:

• Have solid professional software development experience and a university degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Have strong software engineering fundamentals and can independently solve complex technical problems.

• Are comfortable understanding and navigating established codebases and architectures.

• Care about maintainability, reliability, security, and long-term software quality.

• Can reason about technical trade-offs and communicate your decisions clearly.

• Enjoy technical collaboration, constructive discussions, and helping other developers grow.

• Are curious about AI-assisted development and interested in improving your engineering workflows.

For this particular team, we would especially value:

• Strong experience with C# and .NET.

• Experience improving or modernizing established software systems.

• Understanding of Domain-Driven Design, modular architecture, or similar approaches to organizing complex applications.

• Experience contributing to architectural decisions and technical direction.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in Orthopaedic Surgery - Knee Surgery
jobs.description:
A position as Assistant Professor (35% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Orthopaedic Surgery, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark.  The position is combined with an employment at Odense University Hospital.

The position is limited to 4 years.

The research unit

The Research Unit of Orthopaedic Surgery provides a dynamic and multidisciplinary research environment and is engaged in a broad range of research activities. Our research spans clinical and experimental as well as epidemiological research, including registry-based research and accident analysis.

Our team consists of both scientific and technical/administrative staff, including professors, postdoctoral researchers, PhD students, research nurses, secretaries and a laboratory technician.

We have extensive collaborations with other medical specialties and research groups, both nationally and internationally, fostering interdisciplinary research and knowledge exchange.

Research tasks

• 
Serve as project lead for the REPLAN research project, with responsibility for its scientific direction, coordination, and overall progress. The REPLAN project investigates whether routine patellar resurfacing reduces patient dissatisfaction and knee pain compared with non-resurfacing in contemporary primary total knee arthroplasty. 

• 
Supervise a PhD student, including providing scientific guidance and supporting the progress and completion of the PhD project.

• 
Prepare and publish scientific manuscripts in peer-reviewed international journals and present research findings at national and international conferences.

Teaching tasks

• 
Contribute to teaching medical students and clinical biomechanics students within orthopaedic surgery, with particular emphasis on knee surgery. 

Expectations and qualifications

The job involves research, professional development, research education, research-based teaching, including exams, supervision within the field of knee surgery. 

The candidate who is hired must complete a Lecturer Training Programme during the period of employment.

The assistant professor must have documented research experience within the area of knee arthroplasty. 

In addition, good cooperation skills are expected in order to further the development of research in the areas mentioned above, both interdisciplinary as well as nationally and internationally. International partners are an advantage, but not a requirement.

Research strategy for OUH and the Department of Clinical Research

The joint research strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital sets the direction for our shared research efforts in the years ahead. Rooted in the vision –We conduct research together to shape the patient care of the future – it focuses in particular on: cross-disciplinary research – with people at the centre; strong research environments – as drivers of development; and the research journey – from idea to impact. Further information on the joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital is available here.

Further information

Further information about the position can be obtained from Head of Research at The Research Unit of Orthopaedic Surgery, Martin Lindberg-Larsen, e-mail: martin.lindberg-larsen@rsyd.dk, phone: +45 2521 3900 or Head of Department of Clinical Research, Rikke Leth-Larsen, e-mail: rllarsen@health.sdu.dk, phone: +45 6550 3477.

Application deadline

December 08, 2026, at 23.59 hrs. (CET/CEST).

Salary and terms of employment

The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Assistant Professor is placed within salary steps 4–8 of the Danish state salary scale, depending on seniority. In addition, a centrally agreed assistant professor allowance is paid, and further qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Odense University Hospital, J.B. Winsløws Vej 4, 5000 Odense C.   

Application

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below.

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

• 
a motivation letter

• 
a detailed CV

• 
degree certificates (MsC and Ph.D.-diploma)

• 
a complete and numbered list of publications

• 
3 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file.

• 
It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file.

• 
a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

• 
a research plan detailing the candidate’s ideas and plans for her/his future research work

• 
An explanation other qualification relevant to the post

For technical issues, please contact: hcm-support@sdu.dk

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application.  

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered.

Assessment

Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: Backend Software Developer - Team Sports Applications
jobs.description:
**Job Description

**Do you want to develop cutting-edge software applications for our world-leading products? Looking to use and grow your development skills in a fast-paced and creative environment? If this sounds like an exciting challenge, we’d love to hear from you!

About The Job Trackman products generate extremely accurate measurements using a patented combination of camera and radar, which provide valuable insights for athletes ranging from top worldclass professionals to enthusiastic amateurs, as well as coaches, scouts, and clubs of all levels.

As part of our company's continued expansion, we are looking for a .NET C# backend developer. You will join a department of 45+ skilled developers, responsible for applications used in golf, baseball, softball and football. You will be part of refinement, planning, implementation, testing and deployment to our customers.

We build applications hosted on distributed Linux servers running Docker, on Microsoft Azure technologies, on mobile devices and customer laptops. You will get to interact with skilled developers working across a range of platforms and apps. We always work with the latest LTS .NET version using C# with web frontends in React.

As part of our development toolkit, our teams actively use AI-assisted tools such as GitHub Copilot and Claude to speed up coding, testing, and documentation — letting our developers spend more time on solving interesting problems and less on repetitive tasks.

You will join a team of skilled developers who love what they do and, in a role, where you can have a big impact both on what is being built and how it is built. We value having our developers being part of refinement and you will be deeply involved in finding great solutions from a technical as well as a user perspective together with our Head of Products and UI/UX designers.

• 3+ years of working with .NET and excellent C# programming skills

• Professional usage of an IDE like Visual Studio or Rider

• Work in an agile environment with a strong focus on collaboration, knowledge sharing, and clear communication

• Good understanding of architectural patterns and software design principles

• Good communication skills and a positive and proactive mindset

• Experience with Git

Additional skills (not required, but nice to have):

• Experience with using AI-assisted development tools (e.g. GitHub Copilot, Claude)

• Experience with Docker and Azure Pipelines

All we ask is that you bring passion, curiosity and structure to our workplace. We are a company of many nationalities. Whether you are from abroad or already living in Denmark, we welcome talented people of any gender, nationality and belief. We think the right mix of people makes for the best culture and product.

At Trackman, we see AI not as a replacement for great developers, but as a tool that makes great developers even more effective — accelerating code reviews, catching bugs earlier, and freeing up time for the creative problem-solving that moves our products forward.

The IT landscape is evolving faster than ever and staying up to date with AI-assisted development is quickly becoming a fundamental part of the software development process.

The cherry on top is our canteen: with an indoor and outdoor area to enjoy the fresh food prepared by our own kitchen staff.

**Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

**Where innovation happens

**At Trackman, we know that great people make great products. We believe that teams thrive, and innovation sparks in an atmosphere where people are encouraged to think for themselves, where everybody’s voices are heard, and where the best ideas prevail in the pursuit of exceptional solutions. This mix makes Trackman an inspiring company – for our customers and colleagues.

**Share our Passion!

jobs.description:
_Please do not contact us or apply if you are a recruiter, consultant, or outsourcing company.

_Join a team of fintech heroes! 🚀

Performativ is changing the way investment advisors and financial institutions operate. We are building a modern platform for portfolio management, reporting, compliance, trading, and client engagement—replacing fragmented systems, manual workflows, and technology built for another era.

Our customers include wealth managers, asset managers, family offices, and financial institutions across Europe and beyond. We are on an ambitious scaling journey, supported by leading global venture capital investors, and are working to become the platform on which modern wealth management runs.

You can read more about our product at performativ.com.

As our new Senior Software Engineer — Wealth Management Systems 📈

You will help the team solve some of the hardest product and data problems across Performativ’s investment platform.

You will work where financial workflows, product decisions, and technical systems meet: portfolio data, reporting, fees, reconciliation, instruments, transactions, cash, performance, and trading. Your contribution will be turning that complexity into coherent solutions that work across customers rather than becoming a collection of one-off customisations.

This is not a narrowly scoped position. We work as one team, and you should be willing to tackle any important problem within our area.

• You will apply deep experience from wealth management, asset management, private banking, portfolio management, investment operations, trading, custody, or related financial infrastructure to develop sound product and system designs.

• You will investigate problems that cross financial data, calculations, APIs, integrations, operational processes, and production systems—determining their root causes and delivering reliable solutions that others can understand and extend.

Experience with performance calculations, valuations, fees, reporting, reconciliation, corporate actions, or portfolio-management systems would be particularly valuable.

We value your passion 🔥

At Performativ, we are builders first. We have ambitious goals and value the time, judgment, and effort people put into their work. You will be trusted to make your mark and help shape how we solve difficult problems.

We do not divide the platform into personal territories. People develop deeper context in different areas, but we solve problems as a team. Autonomy works only when paired with initiative, collaboration, sound judgment, and follow-through.

AI increases our delivery speed, but it does not reduce our engineering standard or our accountability for the result. You must be technically strong enough to recognise weak abstractions, incorrect assumptions, missing edge cases, security problems, and unsafe production behaviour.

While working from our Headquarters in Ballerup, Copenhagen area, you will join a global team of colleagues across Denmark, Germany, USA, and Asia, and you will report directly to our NPI Manager, based in Ballerup.

The opportunity

Etac is a global leader in innovative assistive devices, dedicated to enabling people to live active and independent lives. Our Export organisation supports a global network of distributors, served by Customer Service teams in Denmark, Sweden and Austria.

Today, those teams operate independently, each with its own processes, systems and service standards. The next step is clear: one integrated Export Customer Service organisation, built to scale. We are now hiring an Export Customer Service Manager to lead that integration and own the result.

You have led this kind of transformation before. You know how to harmonize teams, processes and performance without losing the expertise and engagement that made each team successful.

Your mission

You step into an evolving function with experienced people and clear ambitions. Your mandate: build one coordinated, scalable Export Customer Service organization. Within 12-18 months, you will have delivered:

• 
One team across Denmark, Sweden and Austria, with clear roles, ownership and escalation paths.

• 
Harmonized workflows, consistent service standards, and KPIs that show how we really perform.

• 
A ticketing and case management solution that is live, adopted and used every day, building on the project plan already in place.

The role

As Export CSM, you lead the Export Customer Service teams across three countries, a team of ~10 professionals.

The role is primarily people leadership and change, complemented by hands-on operational involvement. You set the direction, roll up your sleeves when it counts, and make sure every distributor gets a consistent and proactive experience.

You report directly to Nikolaj Takla, Managing Director Export and work closely with Sales, Supply Chain, Logistics and Product Management.

Your key responsibilities

• 
Lead, coach and engage experienced CS professionals across countries and cultures.

• 
Harmonize processes and define clear roles, responsibilities, and ownership.

• 
Introduce service levels, operational KPIs and transparent performance reporting where little exists today.

• 
Drive the implementation and adoption of the new ticketing and case management solution.

• 
Improve workflows, workload distribution and resource planning; cut manual admin and open the door to automation and self-service.

• 
Strengthen the order-to-delivery chain through tight collaboration with Sales, Supply Chain and Logistics.

• 
Balance one standard with the needs of local markets and distributors.

Your profile

You are a builder and can challenge established ways of working and bring people on board with you. You create clarity fast, decide when it is needed, and build trust through consistency rather than control. You read cultures well, because what works in Gedved does not automatically land in Sweden or Austria. And you like pragmatic solutions. Besides, you have:

• 
5+ years in Customer Service, Customer Operations, Sales Support or a comparable function, including people leadership, ideally across locations or countries.

• 
A proven track record of leading Customer Service through transformation: harmonizing, centralizing or integrating teams from a fragmented starting point. This is not your first change journey.

• 
Hands-on experience setting up KPIs, service levels and reporting, and implementing or optimizing Customer Service systems, preferably ticketing or case management.

• 
Solid understanding of order-to-delivery in an international B2B environment. Experience with distributor networks and manufacturing, medical devices, assistive technology or other product-driven industries is a strong plus.

• 
Professional fluency in English. Danish, Swedish or German is an advantage.

What's in it for you

• 
Real impact, real lives. Your work shows up in the daily lives of the people who rely on our products, and in every distributor who gets a faster, clearer answer.

• 
A mandate to build. You own the operating model: structure, KPIs, tooling and ways of working, including taking a planned ticketing and case management solution from draft to daily use

• 
International scope. Daily collaboration across Denmark, Sweden, Austria and our global distributor network.

• 
The package. Competitive salary, solid pension plan and the flexibility of hybrid working, with a regular office presence either in Gedved (Denmark) or Anderstorp (Sweden).

Why Etac

We are a dynamic company on an exciting journey, with job opportunities in several career fields and many parts of the world. As part of our team, you will work in a place that values:

• 
Working with something that helps people

• 
Possibilities to grow within one's role and the organisation

• 
Good work-life balance

• 
Freedom with responsibility

Interested?

Submit your CV by 14-12-2026 at the latest. If you would like to hear more about the position, please contact Christa Buss, TA Consultant via email at extchbu@etac.com].

Etac is committed to building diverse teams. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and life experiences.

About Etac

Etac is a world-leading developer of innovative assistive devices and patient handling equipment. Since 1973, we have been committed to improving quality of life for the individual, family members and caregivers.

Through our specialised product brands, we offer state-of-the-art solutions for a wide range of daily needs and care settings, for people at all stages of life. Headquartered in Sweden, Etac is a global company with around 1 500 employees, sales in over 80 countries and a revenue of approximately EUR 500 million.

jobs.occupation: Researcher of Active Matter and Mechanobiology at the Niels Bohr Institute
jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic researcher who will work on the collective arrow of time and information flow in active multicellular matter to commence 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position is part of our research on the collective arrow of time and information flow in active multicellular matter. The project combines theoretical and data driven investigation of collective multicellular organization, with potential applications in the life sciences.

  Information on the department can be found at: www.nbi.ku.dk  

   

  Our research
 Active matter comprises a wide range of living systems including cells, bacteria, and subcellular filaments, as well as artificial and synthetic materials that are continuously driven far from equilibrium by their constituent elements. Fundamental biological processes such as cell division, cell death, and the emergence of coordinated motion of cells are governed by the activation of biochemical signals by mechanical stresses and by the physics of active matter. Our group works as an interdisciplinary team at the interface of physics and biology, in collaboration with experimental groups.

   

  Your job 
 Your project will address the collective arrow of time and information flow in active multicellular matter. You will use theoretical and data driven approaches to investigate collective multicellular organization, with potential applications in the life sciences.

  The researcher’s responsibilities will primarily consist of: 

   	
• research, including obligations with regard to publication and scientific communication  	
• research-based teaching with associated examination obligations  	
• to a limited extent, other duties     

  Profile 
 General criteria apply to the appointment of Researchers at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, innovation and societal impact, organisational contribution, and leadership) are considered a framework for the overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement. Find the criteria for Researchers here: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5a_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-Assistant_professors.pdf.

  Furthermore, we are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following skills and experience:

  Essential experience and skills:

   	
• You have a PhD in physics 	
• You have established knowledge of both theoretical and experimental active matter and mechanobiology

Copenhagen / Brøndby, Denmark | HX Product Design, 100% dedicated to a new product.

Make an impact with us

Help shape a new product at Milestone Systems, where what you do matters and people are at the heart of everything we do. You will bring curiosity and continuous learning to an environment grounded in integrity, collaboration and strong relationships.

Help decide what our new product becomes. As a founding product designer, fully dedicated to the initiative, you will work directly with customers and a small Product and Engineering team. Together, you will discover what matters, build working experiments and turn promising ideas into well-crafted experiences.

About the role

We have an early thesis; the customer problems, product scope and workflows are still open. You will help define the product itself, starting with empathy for customers to discover opportunities and frame problems before requirements exist. With Product and Engineering, you will make assumptions explicit, create hypotheses and test them with customers to decide where to invest next.

You will work alongside Product and Engineering from discovery through delivery, building and learning together rather than through sequential handoffs. Together, you will agree ownership and decision rights, so your responsibilities and autonomy are clear. You will report to Damion Bailey, the Head of Product Design.

What you will do

• 
Discover problems worth solving. Personally interview and observe operators, administrators and purchase or adoption stakeholders, focusing on customers facing active problems or real purchase/adoption decisions. Use what you learn to establish which problems merit investment and shape product direction with Product and Engineering.

• 
Build to learn. Independently create functional, code-based experiments using AI-assisted tools, real data and available platform capabilities. Agree learning questions and evidence thresholds, critically review AI output and decide what to pursue, change or stop.

• 
Design and test human + AI interactions. Explore new modalities and interaction patterns that make intelligent systems understandable, balancing automation, transparency, attention and human oversight and control.

• 
Turn learning into customer value. Take validated opportunities toward customer-used pilots and shipped capabilities with Product and Engineering, agreeing feasible milestones and making trade-offs explicit.

• 
Craft experiences that last. Bring interaction design, accessibility and visual detail to production. Let principles and reusable patterns emerge from learning, creating coherence across the initiative and wider Milestone ecosystem.

What success looks like

• 
First weeks: Meet customers directly and begin timeboxed experiments. Agree what each experiment needs to teach you, what evidence will be sufficient to make a decision and when that decision will be made.

• 
Within 60–90 days: Show how customer observations and experiments have changed product decisions and the roadmap.

• 
As opportunities mature: Move validated ideas toward customer-used pilots and shipped capabilities, recording adoption, operational value and remaining uncertainty.

• 
What matters: Reduced uncertainty and validated customer value—not prototype volume or polish alone.

What you bring

Your work matters more than your credentials. No specific degree is required. We look for portfolio evidence and shipped outcomes across four core areas: customer-grounded discovery, independent AI-native building, zero-to-one product judgment and end-to-end design craft. Alongside these, we look for the collaboration, English-language and mobility requirements described under Working together.

• 
Customer-grounded discovery. You have personally interviewed and observed customers, identified opportunities and designed experiments that changed product direction.

• 
Functional, code-based prototyping. You can independently build working prototypes with AI-assisted tools, critically assess the tools’ output and collaborate with engineers at implementation depth. This is what we mean by independent AI-native building.

• 
Zero-to-one product judgment. You have repeatedly helped small, autonomous teams turn uncertain needs into live pilots, shipped capabilities or real adoption decisions. You can explain your contribution, trade-offs and decisions to pursue, change or stop.

• 
End-to-end design craft. You combine interaction design, accessibility, visual craft and systems thinking to make complex, intelligent systems intuitive and trustworthy, with appropriate transparency and human control.

• 
Working together. You collaborate confidently across disciplines, conduct research and communicate in professional English, and are willing to co-locate with the founding team in Copenhagen and travel for customer or partner testing during critical phases.

OPTIONAL (helpful, not required): experience with AI products, enterprise or operational workflows, platform ecosystems, video/security technology, or semiotics and non-verbal communication.

Why this opportunity

You will have direct customer access and close partnership with product and engineering decision-makers. This gives you the opportunity to combine customer discovery, AI-native building and design craft, with learning that helps shape the initiative and influence the next generation of Milestone products.

How you can grow

• 
Deepen your expertise in zero-to-one product creation, AI-native design and product strategy through hands-on founding-team work.

• 
Explore potential development paths toward principal-level experience design or broader product design leadership.

Ready to make an impact?

Excited by the chance to shape what comes next? We would love to see how you think, learn and build.

Apply with your CV and portfolio in English. In your portfolio examples, explain your personal contribution, the customer evidence and the key trade-offs. Show the path from discovery and working experiments to a pilot, shipped capability or adoption decision. An example where evidence led you to stop or substantially redirect an idea is also welcome.

Help us evolve the technical foundation for digital manufacturing at VELUX. As IIoT Platform Technical Lead, you will lead the technical direction of our shared IIoT platform while taking part in engineering. You will enable development teams to build manufacturing applications through reliable connectivity, standardised shop floor data and reusable platform services.

Meet your future team

You will join the Industrial IoT Platform Team, part of IT & Digital Enablement. The team develops and maintains the shared IIoT platform that supports manufacturing applications through connectivity, data and reusable technical capabilities.

As IIoT Platform Technical Lead, you will provide day-to-day technical leadership across the engineering group. Working closely with senior IIoT platform engineers, architects, vendors and manufacturing stakeholders, you will coordinate decisions, coach engineers and help move delivery forward. The role has no formal people-management responsibility.

What We Offer

This role combines contributing to the shared IIoT platform’s technical direction with direct engineering work. You will lead day-to-day technical direction and engineering execution, contributing to design, development, testing, reviews and complex problem-solving. You will turn product priorities into a coherent platform roadmap, engineering practices and clear guardrails.

You will balance a clear technical direction with close collaboration, involving the team in technical decisions and finding practical compromises that support both platform integrity and delivery needs.

The goal in this role means a clear and maintained platform roadmap, faster onboarding and greater reuse, improved visibility of platform health, and well-defined ownership between shared platform capabilities and domain-specific application logic.

More specifically your tasks will be to:

• Own and maintain the IIoT platform technical roadmap, including runtime, frameworks, connectivity components, data contracts, developer tooling, observability and lifecycle enablers. Provide estimates, sequencing, dependency and risk input and coordinate with dependent product teams.

• Coordinate technical planning, reviews and coaching across the platform engineering group, aligning key design decisions with senior IIoT platform engineers. Act as the first technical escalation point. Guide external engineering contributions so standards, knowledge and lifecycle accountability remain within the team. Escalate material architecture and cross-platform decisions through the appropriate technical governance.

• Establish and evolve engineering guardrails, reference patterns and clear development paths. Maintain the boundary between shared platform mechanisms and domain-specific application logic. Own technical data-quality controls at the platform boundary.

• Contribute hands-on to platform services and reusable components through design, development, testing and improvement. Focus your direct contribution where technical depth, complex problem-solving or delivery needs require it.

• Support platform observability, technical investigations and follow-through on incidents, problems and improvement actions in collaboration with the Operations Manager.

• Manage platform lifecycle health, including security, patching, vulnerability remediation, upgrades, documentation, supportability, and technical debt.

The role can be based in Skjern, Østbirk, Kolding or Hørsholm. Regular on-site presence in Skjern and at manufacturing locations in Denmark is required, along with occasional international travel. When tasks and projects allow, you may work from home up to two days per week.

What You Will Bring Into The Organization

You bring 7+ years of relevant experience in software, platform or integration engineering, including technical leadership in an industrial IT/OT or digital manufacturing environment. You understand both manufacturing-domain needs and Unified Namespace. You use that understanding to make technical choices that work for platform users and the engineering team.

Moreover, we expect that you:

• Have direct experience building C#/.NET services and APIs. Your experience also includes event-driven or decoupled architectures, Unified Namespace, containerised deployment and modern DevOps practices.

• Bring practical knowledge across industrial connectivity and edge technologies, including MQTT, edge runtimes and container orchestration. You also understand industrial data contracts, observability or SRE practices, and OT cyber security.

• Can translate product priorities into an actionable platform roadmap, technical guardrails and engineering practices.

• Can make practical technical design decisions while involving engineers and relevant stakeholders in finding workable solutions.

• Use effective coaching, facilitation, collaboration and communication skills across engineers, product roles, architects, vendors and manufacturing stakeholders.

• Apply a platform mindset focused on reuse, self-service, consumer enablement, operational excellence and long-term maintainability.
